linear.text: Observation: Indentation crack path shows deflection, bridging, grain pull-out and branching into a SiC-rich region  [panels F8f]
Mechanism that produces it: Interlocked ZrB2 platelets and nano SiC trigger pull-out, crack bridging, deflection and branching, lengthening the crac  [premise: k5]
What it explains: Hardness, flexural strength and toughness rise then fall with ZrSi2, peaking at RZSZ-20 (17.1 GPa, 655 MPa, 6.08 MPa m1/

traces.question: Given the background on this reactive-hot-pressed ZrB2-SiC system and its interlocking-platelet microstructure described above, and given panel 10.1007/s40145-019-0334-4#F8f showing the indentation crack path (deflection, bridging, grain pull-out and branching into a SiC-rich region), what mechanism is responsible for this crack behavior?
traces.answer_key: The interlocked ZrB2 platelets together with the nano-scale SiC force grain pull-out, crack bridging, deflection and branching, which lengthens the crack path (m2). The deflection specifically into the SiC-rich region is aided by tangential tensile residual stress left around SiC grains by the ZrB2/SiC thermal-expansion mismatch, as reported in the cited reference (k5) -- but this thermal-mismatch effect on its own is only a contributing premise, not the full explanation; the platelet interlocking plus nano-SiC is the operative mechanism.
traces.grading: Certified judge against the graph's mechanism node m2 (interlocked platelets and nano-SiC driving pull-out, bridging, deflection and branching) and its premise k5 (thermal-expansion-mismatch residual stress), with the rival mechanism node m3 named as the alternative explanation the judge must confirm is not sufficient on its own.
